## Natural history notes

A medium-sized heron characterized by its slender body, long neck, bluish-gray plumage as an adult, and dark-tipped bill with a bluish base. Juveniles are mostly white and can resemble egrets, but they gradually molt into the darker adult plumage. In Florida, it is found in marshes, swamps, ponds, mangroves, tidal flats, wet prairies, and shallow coastal or freshwater wetlands. It feeds mainly on small fish, frogs, crayfish, insects, and other aquatic animals, usually hunting by slowly stalking through shallow water or standing still before striking with its bill.
